A_general.license: N/A for the closed hosted server; the public repository is a documentation repository.
other_official_servers: https://aa-mcp.adobe.io/mcp — Adobe Analytics reporting MCP server.

https://mcp-gateway.adobe.io/cja/mcp — CJA endpoint shown in general server and OAuth documentation; the CJA-specific server page and client setup guide identify the input endpoint, https://cja-mcp.adobe.io/mcp.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Adobe says the Analytics MCP servers have no additional cost for Adobe Analytics and CJA customers. MCP report calls count toward the organization's existing monthly report request allowance.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: NOT FOUND; the reviewed official MCP FAQ does not state CJA subscription prices or plan names.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: No MCP-specific charge is documented. Reporting calls consume the existing monthly report request allowance; Adobe says organizations can contact their account team about increasing that allowance.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires Adobe OAuth and an applicable MCP permission item plus underlying CJA permissions. Read-only access permits discovery and reports; Full Access is required for component creation or updates. Product administrators automatically have full access. Report results are limited to 100 rows per call with no pagination parameter.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Adobe controls the hosted service and OAuth; organization administrators assign product profiles and permissions; the user's existing product permissions also apply.

The supplied endpoint returned HTTP 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=https://cja-mcp.adobe.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. Both protected-resource documents report resource https://cja-mcp.adobe.io/mcp, bearer_methods_supported [header], scopes_supported [openid, AdobeID, additional_info.projectedProductContext], and authorization_servers [https://cja-mcp.adobe.io]. The authorization-server document reports response_types_supported [code], code_challenge_methods_supported [S256], grant_types_supported [authorization_code], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [none], registration_endpoint https://cja-mcp.adobe.io/register, token_endpoint https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/token/v3, authorization_endpoint https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/authorize/v2, revocation_endpoint https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/revoke, and scopes_supported [openid, AdobeID, additional_info.projectedProductContext]. OpenID configuration returned HTTP 500 NoResourceFoundException. Adobe docs also describe OAuth DCR for supported clients and server-to-server OAuth; docs say token lifetime is the expires_in value. The metadata does not specify a lifetime.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: 401 challenge identifies Bearer resource metadata; authorized response structure is not published in the reviewed material.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth protected-resource metadata and authorization-server metadata; authorization_code grant with PKCE S256; client authentication method none; dynamic registration at https://cja-mcp.adobe.io/register. Supported scopes: openid, AdobeID, additional_info.projectedProductContext. Bearer token in header. Revocation endpoint https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/revoke. Token lifetime not stated in metadata; Adobe says to use expires_in from token response. Adobe docs additionally describe server-to-server client_credentials access tokens.
C_capabilities.authorization_server: https://cja-mcp.adobe.io (issuer); authorization and token endpoints are hosted at https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official reference distinguishes discovery/reporting tools from component creation and updates. It does not publish tool annotations such as readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint. 2. No required confirmation parameter or server-enforced preview/confirmation workflow is documented. Tool-specific guide calls and validations are described, but the reference does not say they are enforced prerequisites. 3. OAuth metadata exposes scopes openid, AdobeID, and additional_info.projectedProductContext. Adobe product profiles grant MCP Read-only or MCP Full Access, with underlying CJA permissions also enforced; permissions combine across profiles. Product administrators automatically receive full access. Metadata specifies authorization_code, PKCE S256, DCR, bearer header, and revocation URL; token lifetime is unspecified. 4. Read-only/full-access permission tiers exist. No toolset/readonly URL filter is documented. Adobe says current URLs route requests to the nearest region based on IMS org; one IMS org is active at a time in a client connection. 5. Adobe states the LLM can access the same data the user is authorized to see. CJA governance may label sensitive data and add warnings or labels to exported reports; specific MCP field masking is not documented. 6. MCP calls consume the monthly report request allowance. runReport returns up to 100 rows per call and has no pagination parameter. Lookup tools document pagination and per-call maximums. 7. Public implementation code is unavailable. Official parameter tables define inputs; correction, coercion, unknown-argument rejection, or operator overrides are not documented. 8. Server logging, audit records, telemetry payloads, and opt-out are not documented. 9. The official reference/changelog tool names include no feedback/rating/survey tools; no MCP upsell message is documented. The broader guide instructs customers to assess integration risks. 10. describeCja provides workflow guides; Adobe Skills are separately installed client-side. Documentation contains recommendations to call describeCja before selected workflows, but no hosted code is available to establish enforcement. 11. setDefaultSessionDataViewId stores session state for up to eight hours; tools can use this default. Component search ranking uses recent and frequent personal and organization usage history. 12. Adobe documents separate Adobe Analytics and CJA servers; the CJA endpoint is a flat tool reference. The skills are separate client-side instructions. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script execution tool appears in the official CJA tool reference or changelog.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The CJA service is documented as one hosted endpoint with a flat collection of tools. Adobe also operates a separate Adobe Analytics endpoint; separately distributed skills run on top of the CJA server.

Adobe's official changelog also names getCalculatedMetricFunctions and validateCalculatedMetric, absent from that reference; these are added as official tools with unpublished parameters where applicable. No official stated total was found. No catalogue-only tools were added. Claude's Anthropic-verified connector page lists 26 humanized tool names; Developers Digest says 15 tools; Obot documents capabilities but no tool count. Catalogue counts differ from the official docs and changelog.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted implementation and verbatim initialize/tool-list payload are unavailable; documentation descriptions cannot establish the actual pre-interaction context.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Adobe says MCP does not currently make admin changes such as editing data views or managing report suites, and does not support scheduled report delivery; it recommends the CJA UI for scheduled delivery. Adobe's FAQ says runReport lacks pagination and returns at most 100 rows per call. Sources: https://developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/support/faq and https://developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/cja/reference

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Adobe recommends: "Apply filters or narrow your query scope to work within this limit." For malformed project definitions, it says: "Provide the LLM with an existing valid project as a reference before prompting it to create a new one." Adobe also recommends clients call describeCja before selected workflows; the documentation does not establish that these recommendations are server-enforced.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Adobe says MCP access is controlled through product profiles and that MCP servers enforce users' existing product permissions. It states the connected LLM "can access the same data that the user is authorized to see." Adobe recommends reviewing the LLM provider's data-handling policies; data use for model training depends on the provider agreement. The CJA governance documentation says sensitive-data labels and policies may surface in data views and exports.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Adobe states the MCP servers make no LLM calls themselves and call only Adobe Analytics and CJA APIs. Adobe says the MCP service has no additional cost for customers, though report calls use the existing allowance.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission enforcement and report row limits are documented server behavior. The FAQ's no-LLM-calls statement is a vendor description of service architecture, but public server code is unavailable for independent verification. Recommendations to review provider terms, test in a sandbox, validate actions, and narrow queries are guidance rather than documented server controls. MCP-specific logging, retention, and telemetry behavior were not found.

contradictions: Adobe's CJA tool reference describes itself as a complete list and names 27 tools, while the official October 19, 2026 changelog separately announces getCalculatedMetricFunctions and validateCalculatedMetric; the reference does not list either. Both changelog-named tools are included in actions.json.

Adobe's general server and OAuth documentation show https://mcp-gateway.adobe.io/cja/mcp, while the supplied endpoint, CJA-specific server page, and client setup docs use https://cja-mcp.adobe.io/mcp. The supplied endpoint's own OAuth metadata and HTTP 401 evidence identify the analysis target.

Claude's connector directory lists 26 humanized tool names, whereas the official reference lists 27 exact names plus the two tools named in the changelog. Developers Digest reports 15 tools. These catalogue totals do not match the official sources.
observations_for_research: The default session data view is mutable session state and is documented to persist up to eight hours.
Dimension and metric discovery can use semantic search; results can be ranked by recent and frequent personal and organization usage.
Adobe documents separate read-only and full-access permission items, with underlying product permissions also applying.
Some guide tool descriptions direct agents to consult documentation before selected write or multi-step tasks.
The official reference and changelog disagree on completeness of the current tool inventory.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, all indexed page text and relevant HTML-backed official reference pages, and the local AdobeDocs/analytics-mcp repository. The local repository is documentation-only, not endpoint implementation; the Adobe Skills repository is client-side skills rather than server code. The Adobe tool-reference link had an automated plausibility warning because the page text did not mention the product name, but the page title, description, content, repository path, and CJA-specific docs confirm its relevance. No official CJA price schedule, MCP-specific privacy terms, release-status label, protocol-version declaration, annotations, or hosted initialize output was found. The pre-fetched OpenID configuration returned HTTP 500. Unofficial server evidence was not used.
